        client-Java engine — synchronizer, compiler, ClassConsumer SPI, controller routing) and
        components/engine/engine-bpm-flowable (only needs to resolve client-compiled classes from
        delegate expressions). Extracted from engine-java's runtime package so engine-bpm-flowable
        can depend on this small leaf module instead of the full engine — that in turn lets
        components/api/api-modules-java publish the org.eclipse.dirigible.sdk.* annotations to
        engine-java without forming a cycle through api-bpm.

se.deversity.vibetags:vibetags-bom 1.1.0 发布, Bill of Materials for the VibeTags annotation processor. Import this BOM to get
        a coherent vibetags-annotations + vibetags-processor pair without specifying
        each version individually.

        Recommended setup — annotations on the compile classpath, processor on the
        annotation-processor path only (the processor jar pulls in slf4j/logback,
        which has no business on consumer code's compileClasspath):

        Maven:
            <dependencyManagement>
                <dependencies>
                    <dependency>
                        <groupId>se.deversity.vibetags</groupId>
                        <artifactId>vibetags-bom</artifactId>
                        <version>1.1.0</version>
                        <type>pom</type>
                        <scope>import</scope>
                    </dependency>
                </dependencies>
            </dependencyManagement>

        Gradle:
            implementation platform('se.deversity.vibetags:vibetags-bom:1.1.0')
            annotationProcessor platform('se.deversity.vibetags:vibetags-bom:1.1.0')
            compileOnly 'se.deversity.vibetags:vibetags-annotations'
            annotationProcessor 'se.deversity.vibetags:vibetags-processor'

items.summary:
se.deversity.vibetags:vibetags-bom 1.1.0 发布, Bill of Materials for the VibeTags annotation processor. Import this BOM to get
        a coherent vibetags-annotations + vibetags-processor pair without specifying
        each version individually.

        Recommended setup — annotations on the compile classpath, processor on the
        annotation-processor path only (the processor jar pulls in slf4j/logback,
        which has no business on consumer code's compileClasspath):

        Maven:
            <dependencyManagement>
                <dependencies>
                    <dependency>
                        <groupId>se.deversity.vibetags</groupId>
                        <artifactId>vibetags-bom</artifactId>
                        <version>1.1.0</version>
                        <type>pom</type>
                        <scope>import</scope>
                    </dependency>
                </dependencies>
            </dependencyManagement>

        Gradle:
            implementation platform('se.deversity.vibetags:vibetags-bom:1.1.0')
            annotationProcessor platform('se.deversity.vibetags:vibetags-bom:1.1.0')
            compileOnly 'se.deversity.vibetags:vibetags-annotations'
            annotationProcessor 'se.deversity.vibetags:vibetags-processor'

        artifact that reaches a consuming project's compile classpath, which is why it is an artifact of
        its own rather than a package inside airness-config: folding it in would put the analyzer
        configurations on that classpath as well, to no purpose.

        not survive compilation into the consumer's artifact.

eu.ciechanowiec:airness-assets 1.0.3 发布, The files the harness owns but cannot supply from a classpath, and the manifest saying what a
        project may do with each.

        Most of the harness reaches a project as configuration an analyzer reads off its own plugin
        classpath, which is why most of it needs no file in the project at all. What lands here is what
        something outside Maven reads from disk: an editor reading .editorconfig, git reading
        .gitattributes. Those have nowhere else to live, so they live in the project and are checked
        against the bytes shipped here.

        Each canonical file is stored under an added .asset suffix. A stored .gitignore under its own
        name would be a working .gitignore over this directory and could stop its neighbours from being
        tracked, and a stored .gitattributes would take effect over them. A file that changes the meaning
        of the directory it sits in cannot be stored under its own name.

        files (file presence is the opt-in signal the processor honours), `doctor`

        marker integrity. Run it without installing anything:
